messages:
mia: Heads up — intermittent RX/TX packet jitter and CRC errors on a bunch of p4zn hosts in use1a. Started ~09:04 UTC after the bnxt firmware push to 1.2.3. Not sure if it's correlation or cause.
juan: Which hosts exactly? fleet tag or instance IDs pls.
mia: p4zn-az1-012, p4zn-az1-013, p4zn-az1-014, p4zn-az1-015, p4zn-az1-016. All in the same rack. Quick ifconfig shows increasing rx errors.
ashok: I see the same on five hosts in that rack. Rx error counters climbing over last 30m. Tx drops low.
mia: Paste of ethtool stats from one affected node:
```
# ethtool -S bnxt0 | egrep 'rx_err|tx_err|rx_jab|rx_no_buff'
rx_err: 1245
rx_no_buff: 86
tx_err: 3
rx_jabber: 72
```
kevin: Any related dmesg lines? firmware asserting or a reset loop?
mia: dmesg tail from same node:
```
[1234567.678901] bnxt_en 0000:3b:00.0: FW log: rx_queue_stall
[1234567.679012] bnxt_en 0000:3b:00.0: NIC reset
[1234567.680000] bnxt_en 0000:3b:00.0: firmware version 1.2.3
```
sre-oncall: infra-bot created incident-inc-5332 and added on-call. Auto-escalation to netops.
infra-bot: Incident created: INC-5332 (p4zn bnxt rx_jabber + resets). Priority: P2. Slack channel #inc-5332 created.
juan: Could be jumbo/MTU interacting with offloads. These racks run MTU 9000 by default. Any packet fragmentation or RDMA in use?
ashok: We do have some RDMA flows for Ceph replication in that rack. I'll check rdma_cm logs.
mia: tcpdump snapshot shows lots of L2 retrans and bad checksums coming off the NIC: `tcpdump -i bnxt0 -vv -c 100 'ip'` showed a high ratio of `bad tcp cksum` entries while `ifconfig` shows rx errors.
kevin: To rule out offload issues, can someone flip GRO/GSO/TFO? Quick test command:
```
# disable offloads to test impact
ethtool -K bnxt0 gro off gso off tso off
```
mia: Ran that on a canary node (p4zn-az1-020). Rx errors dropped to near zero after disabling GRO/GSO within 2 minutes. Not definitive but promising.
juan: Good signal. Did you also compare firmware 1.2.2 vs 1.2.3 on identical workload?
mia: I rolled a single canary back to 1.2.2 via bnxt_fw_tool and the errors didn't reproduce for ~45m under same load.
ashok: So likely regression in 1.2.3 interacting with large MTU + offloads + RDMA.
kevin: Netops: can we get vendor confirmation? Also we should not mass-rollback firmware without vendor guidance. Rolling back may impact other fixes.
sre-oncall: Short term mitigations: 1) Disable GRO/GSO/TCO on affected hosts via automation 2) Route Ceph east-west traffic away from that rack 3) Avoid new capacity provisioning on p4zn in use1a until triage complete.
mia: I'll push a runway patch to disable offloads for the affected hostset and add an automation job to revert once vendor/driver fix is out. Patch will be in the maintenance window at 02:00 UTC.
ashok: I'll collect `ethtool -S` and `dmesg` from all affected nodes and upload to the incident S3 bucket. Also capturing `rdma` logs.
juan: Any perf penalty from disabling offloads? Roughly 10-20% CPU increase on net-heavy pods but keeps packets stable. Tradeoff is acceptable for now.
kevin: Start ticket with Broadcom with logs and the canary rollback comparison. Assign to NetEng. Mention MTU=9000 + RDMA + firmware 1.2.3.
infra-bot: Created vendor support case: VND-20478. Uploaded logs bundle.
mia: Action items: 1) Disable offloads (automation) — mia 2) Vendor case & follow up — kevin 3) Collect host logs — ashok 4) Route policy to avoid cluster rack — juan.
sre-oncall: Schedule maintenance window 02:00 UTC, will post customer notice if capacity is impacted.
mia: Will run rollback plan for up to 20 hosts if vendor doesn't provide hotfix by EOD, but prefer vendor patch.
ashok: Adding this to postmortem queue and tagging `networking, firmware, p4zn, mtus`
juan: Thx all. Keep updates in #inc-5332 and drop short notes here if something changes. :eyes:
